newsitem.title: INDIA: Notorious Sobhraj nears release from India jail.
newsitem.headline: Notorious Sobhraj nears release from India jail.

text.p: Notorious criminal Charles Sobhraj took a step toward freedom on Friday after more than two decades in an Indian maximum-security prison, his lawyer said.
New Delhi chief metropolitan magistrate Prem Kumar accepted a 20,000-rupee ($560) surety which Sobhraj provided after winning bail on Thursday in an extradition case.
But the judge turned down a second surety for 10,000 rupees ($280) because it was backed by the same former fellow inmate who furnished the other guarantee, Sobhraj's lawyer Rajan Bakshi said.

Bakshi told Reuters a fresh surety, backed by someone else, would be provided on Saturday afternoon, and Sobhraj, 52, could leave Tihar jail on bail on Saturday evening if the judge accepted the guarantee.
Sobhraj, a French citizen born to an Indian father and a Vietnamese mother, was first arrested in India for holding up a hotel jewellery shop in 1971. He jumped bail before his trial.
India convicted Sobhraj in 1978 of murdering a French tourist. He was acquitted 20 months later on appeal, but remained in Tihar jail on lesser charges.
Another judge sentenced Sobhraj to life imprisonment in 1982 for poisoning an Israeli tourist to death, but again he was acquitted on appeal.
In 1986, Sobhraj escaped while being held pending an extradition request from Thailand to face charges of murder and attempted murder. He was recaptured 24 days later.
Thailand's 20-year statute of limitations later expired and Thai police said late last year that Sobhraj no longer could be tried on their charges.
But Hong Kong police said on Thursday that they still wanted to interview Sobhraj about drugging and robbery cases in the British colony in the 1970s.

Last Friday, an Indian judge granted Sobhraj bail in a case relating to his 1986 jail break. But his release was held up because the government had not told prison authorities that the Thai extradition warrant had lapsed.
Bakshi said on Thursday that he would ask the Delhi High Court in a few days to cancel the Thai warrant.

Bakshi also said a hearing was set for April 30 in the jail-break case, but Sobhraj would not spend more time in jail even if convicted since the maximum penalty would be less than the 11 years he has served since his escape.
On Wednesday, Sobhraj said that after his release he would do social work and might work on a $15-million movie based on his life.
